questions.question: How do you manipulate strings in Ruby?
questions.title: String Manipulation in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Ruby strings have many methods: split (to array), join (array to string), upcase/downcase/capitalize, strip (trim whitespace), sub (first match) and gsub (all matches, with regex), chars (to array of chars), reverse, include?, replace, +, <<. Strings are mutable in older Ruby but frozen by default in 3.0+ for literals; use << or += to build. Common interview moves: split to tokens, gsub with a regex to replace, chars.tally to count, reverse to check a palindrome. Know strings vs symbols: strings are mutable text; symbols are immutable interned labels.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know split/join/gsub/strip/chars/reverse and that strings are text (mutable-ish) vs symbols (immutable labels).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using sub (first only) when you meant gsub (all), or confusing a string with a symbol.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: split/join/gsub/strip/chars/reverse are the common string methods. sub is first-only; gsub is all (regex). Strings are text; symbols are immutable labels.

sections.title: The String Toolkit
sections.content: Ruby strings have many methods: split (to an array), join (array to string), upcase, downcase, capitalize, strip (trim whitespace), sub (replace the first match) and gsub (replace all matches, with a regex), chars (to an array of characters), reverse, include?, replace, +, and <<. Strings are mutable in older Ruby but frozen by default in 3.0 plus for literals; use << or += to build. Common interview moves: split to tokens, gsub with a regex to replace, chars dot tally to count characters, and reverse to check a palindrome. Know strings versus symbols: strings are mutable text; symbols are immutable interned labels used as hash keys or method names.

sections.title: Common String Operations
sections.content:
split, gsub, strip, chars, reverse — the building blocks.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S['a,b,c'] --> Sp[split ','] --> A[['a','b','c']]
  A --> J[join '-'] --> S2['a-b-c']
  S3['  Hi  '] --> St[strip] --> S4['Hi']
```

sections.title: String manipulation
sections.content:
```ruby
s = 'Hello, World'

s.split(', ')            # ['Hello', 'World']
s.split(', ').join('-') # 'Hello-World'

s.upcase                 # 'HELLO, WORLD'
s.downcase               # 'hello, world'
s.strip                 # '  hi  ' -> 'hi'

s.gsub(/[aeiou]/, '*')   # 'H*ll*, W*rld' (all vowels)
s.sub(/l/, 'L')          # 'HeLlo, World' (FIRST match only)

s.chars                 # ['H','e','l','l','o',',',' ','W','o','r','l','d']
s.chars.tally           # {'H'=>1, 'e'=>1, 'l'=>3, ...}
s.reverse               # 'dlroW ,olleH'

# Palindrome check (ignore case + non-letters):
def palindrome?(s)
  clean = s.downcase.gsub(/[^a-z]/, '')
  clean == clean.reverse
end
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using sub (first only) when you meant gsub (all matches).
Confusing a string (mutable text) with a symbol (immutable label).
Forgetting strings are frozen by default in Ruby 3.0+ (use << or += to build).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: split, join, gsub, strip, chars, reverse are the common string methods.
sub replaces the FIRST match; gsub replaces ALL (use a regex).
chars.tally counts characters; reverse flips the string (palindrome check).
Strings are text (mutable-ish, frozen by default in 3.0+); symbols are immutable labels.
Use << or += to build strings; frozen literals can't be mutated in place.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Ruby strings have many methods: split to an array, join an array to a string, upcase, downcase, capitalize, strip to trim whitespace, sub to replace the first match and gsub to replace all matches with a regex, chars to an array of characters, reverse, include, replace, plus, and append. Strings are mutable in older Ruby but frozen by default in 3.0 plus for literals; use append or plus-equals to build. Common interview moves: split to tokens, gsub with a regex to replace, chars dot tally to count characters, and reverse to check a palindrome. Know strings versus symbols: strings are mutable text; symbols are immutable interned labels used as hash keys or method names. A common mistake is using sub, which is first only, when you meant gsub, which is all, and confusing a string with a symbol.
